exposure: Women with recurrent short IPI, recurrent optimal IPI, and single short IPI followed by optimal IPI
recurrent short interpregnancy interval (IPI) (<6 months between the 1st and 2nd pregnancy and the 2nd and 3rd pregnancy)
Second vs. third delivery in women with recurrent short IPI
Recurrent short IPI vs. recurrent optimal IPI
single short IPI (<6 months between the 1st and 2nd pregnancy followed by an optimal IPI of 18-48 months between the 2nd and 3rd pregnancy)
Recurrent short IPI vs. single short IPI followed by optimal IPI
Single short IPI followed by optimal IPI
cohort: 10,569 women who delivered their first three consecutive deliveries in a single tertiary medical center over 20 years
finding: Recurrent short IPI was associated with a higher risk of maternal anemia and small for gestational age neonates compared to both recurrent optimal IPI and single short IPI followed by optimal IPI.
mod_finding: Recurrent short interpregnancy interval was associated with higher rates of in-labor cesarean deliveries in the third pregnancy compared to the second.
birth_weight: Lower in the recurrent short IPI group
